records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Jesus being handed over and taken, as described in John 19:16; the setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus carries a large wooden cross along a rocky path beyond a stone city, with figures behind him and a distant hill beneath a blue sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:17, in which he bears his own cross and goes out to the place called Golgotha. The landscape, figures, and distant crosses are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor scene of Jesus crucified on the central cross, with two other men on crosses on either side, above a rocky landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 19:18: Jesus is crucified between two others, one on each side. The landscape and visual details are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus hangs on a wooden cross beneath a plain wooden plaque, with onlookers and Roman soldiers in a sunlit, rocky landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:19, in which Pilate writes a title and places it on the cross identifying Jesus of Nazareth as King of the Jews. The plaque is shown without lettering.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus is restrained at a stone pillar in a sunlit courtyard as a Roman attendant raises a scourge; Pilate watches from a raised seat.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:1, whose Greek text and Berean Interlinear glosses say that Pilate took Jesus and flogged him. The setting, attendants, and Pilate's presence at the scene are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A crowd looks up at Jesus on the cross and a blank plaque above him, near the stone walls of a city.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:20, where many Jews read the title at the place near the city where Jesus was crucified. The verse says the title was written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek; the plaque is left blank in the image.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several chief priests gesture toward a blank wooden tablet as they speak to Pilate across a table in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:21, where the chief priests ask Pilate to change the wording from the title 'King of the Jews' to the statement that he said he was king. The setting, tablet, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Pilate sits at a table with a blank document and raises a hand firmly toward a visitor, with a Roman guard and a sunlit city behind him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Pilate giving his firm reply in John 19:22: what he has written, he has written. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four soldiers examine garments on a rocky hillside, one holding up a pale woven tunic, with crosses in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 19:23, in which the soldiers divide Jesus' garments into four portions and take his seamless tunic, woven from the top throughout.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four soldiers gather around an intact light-colored garment as one casts lots on the ground; others hold garments, with distant crosses on a hillside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 19:24: the soldiers divide garments and cast lots for the clothing rather than tear it, as the verse says Scripture is fulfilled. The figures, setting, and appearance of the lots are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four women stand closely together beside Jesus on the cross, looking up with sorrow in a rocky landscape beneath a clouded sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 19:25, which places Jesus' mother, his mother's sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene by his cross. The figures' appearances, poses, and landscape are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus looks down from the cross toward his mother and the beloved disciple, who stand together beneath a warm sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:26, where Jesus sees his mother and the disciple he loves standing nearby and tells her to behold her son.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A grieving woman stands beside a compassionate disciple as he welcomes her through the open doorway of a warmly lit home.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the disciple receiving the mother into his own home, inspired by John 19:27. The setting and appearances are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks from the cross on a rocky hillside, with witnesses standing at a distance beneath a cloudy sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:28, when Jesus, knowing all things had been accomplished, says he thirsts so that Scripture might be fulfilled.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man raises a sponge on a leafy stalk to the mouth of Jesus on the cross, while another holds a vessel of dark liquid nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the verse: a sponge filled with sour wine is placed on hyssop and brought to his mouth, with a full vessel nearby. The figures and setting are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Soldiers place a woven crown of thorns on Jesus' head and drape a purple robe around His shoulders as He sits in a stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:2, in which soldiers twist together a crown of thorns, put it on His head, and cast a purple robe around Him.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus hangs on the cross with his head bowed. A soldier holds a sponge nearby, a vessel rests below, and two onlookers stand against a warm, distant landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of John 19:30: after Jesus receives sour wine and says it is finished, he bows his head and yields up his spirit. The setting and surrounding figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jewish petitioners speak solemnly to Pilate in a stone courtyard, while three occupied crosses stand on a distant hill.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of the request to Pilate in John 19:31 on the day of Preparation, before the high Sabbath. The scene depicts the request, not the breaking of legs or removal of the bodies.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Soldiers with wooden clubs attend the legs of two men on crosses on either side of a central crucified figure, in a watercolor landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:32, where the soldiers break the legs of the first man and the other man crucified with Him; the scene's visual details are interpretive.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus hangs with bowed head on a cross, his legs unbroken, as two Roman soldiers look up; one holds a lowered club on a rocky hillside at sunset.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 19:33: those who came to Jesus saw that he was already dead and did not break his legs. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor scene of Jesus on the cross as a soldier raises a spear to His side, where blood and water flow; other figures look on against a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:34, where one soldier pierces His side with a spear and blood and water immediately come out. The setting and onlookers are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man gestures earnestly as he speaks to a group listening beneath a tree, with fields and hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of a witness sharing testimony with listeners reflects the verse’s account of one who has seen and speaks truth so that others may believe.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor scene of Jesus on the cross with his legs intact, above a rocky landscape at sunset; an unlettered scroll rests in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:36: the intact figure and scroll evoke the verse's statement that Scripture was fulfilled and not one of His bones would be broken.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A solemn group looks up at Jesus on the cross, with his pierced side visible, on a rocky hillside above a distant city beneath a warm sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts people looking toward the One they pierced, as described in John 19:37; the setting and figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Joseph of Arimathea carries Jesus' body tenderly through a rocky landscape at sunset, with Jerusalem in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Joseph taking Jesus' body after Pilate gave permission in John 19:38. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Nicodemus carries a jar and a tied bundle along a rocky path toward a rock-cut entrance, with companions and a donkey carrying more bundles and vessels behind him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Nicodemus arriving with the abundant mixture of myrrh and aloes described in John 19:39. The setting, companions, containers and appearance are artistic details; his earlier visit by night is not depicted.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with his hands bound as a man strikes his cheek with an open palm and others mock him in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:3: people come to Jesus, hail him as king of the Jews, and strike him with their palms. The setting, clothing, and individual gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mourners carefully wrap Jesus' body in pale linen on a stone surface, with a bowl of spices nearby, outside a rocky opening in warm evening light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:40, where Jesus' body is bound in linen cloths with spices in preparation for burial; the people and setting are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A flower-filled garden surrounds an open, empty rock-cut tomb, with a wooden cross on a distant hill in warm evening light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the garden at the place where Jesus was crucified and the new tomb in which no one had yet been laid, as described in John 19:41. The garden, tomb, cross, and lighting are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mourners gently lay Jesus, wrapped in linen, on a stone resting place inside a rock-hewn tomb, with a sunlit landscape visible through the entrance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:42, in which they lay Jesus in a nearby tomb because of the Jewish Preparation. The people, setting, and visual details are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Pilate addresses a gathered crowd outside a stone building, gesturing toward Jesus standing in the doorway with guards behind Him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Pilate going outside and announcing that he will bring Jesus out, having found no guilt in Him. The setting, figures, and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands outside a stone doorway wearing a crown of thorns and a purple robe, while a man gestures toward listeners gathered in a courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 19:5: Jesus comes outside wearing the crown of thorns and purple robe, and a speaker presents him to those present. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with his hands bound as chief priests and officers gesture and cry out around him; Pilate addresses them from a seat in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:6, when the chief priests and officers call for Jesus to be crucified and Pilate says he finds no guilt in him. The setting, appearance and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group of Jewish speakers address a seated official in a sunlit stone courtyard while Jesus stands nearby, listening.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the response in John 19:7: the speakers appeal to their law and say that he ought to die because he made himself the Son of God. The setting, gestures, and appearances are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: An apprehensive Pilate sits in a stone hall, listening to a man who gestures toward him, while Roman guards and other figures stand nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:8: Pilate becomes more afraid after hearing a word. The scene, speaker, and setting are artistic details; the verse does not specify the word’s content.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit Roman praetorium, a seated governor extends a questioning hand toward Jesus, who stands silently with his hands bound; guards stand nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 19:9: the governor questions Jesus about where he is from, and Jesus gives him no answer. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At a wedding feast, a bearded steward in a red robe holds a cup of wine and speaks to the smiling bridegroom. Guests dine beneath flowering vines, while a clay jug, cups, grapes, and dishes fill the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 2:10: the master of the feast tells the bridegroom he has kept the good wine until now, although good wine is usually served first and inferior wine after guests have drunk freely. John 2:9 identifies the speaker and the bridegroom. The setting and appearances are imagined. The chapter's English word glosses are uncurated Berean Interlinear glosses, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with attentive disciples beside large stone jars while a servant pours red wine into a cup at a wedding feast in a sunlit courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places Jesus and his disciples at the wedding in Cana, with the stone jars and wine from John 2:1–10. John 2:11 describes this first sign as revealing his glory and says his disciples believed in him. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks down a rocky path beside His mother and four companions toward stone houses by a blue lake.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 2:12 tells that Jesus went down to Capernaum with His mother, His brothers, and His disciples, and that they stayed there not many days. This imaginative scene depicts their arrival; the landscape, appearances, and number of companions are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a stony road toward Jerusalem, with other travelers and the temple visible in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 2:13 describes Passover drawing near and Jesus going up to Jerusalem. This is an imaginative depiction; the road, travelers, and appearance of the city are illustrative details. The token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands in a sunlit temple courtyard among sellers and fenced oxen and sheep. Doves gather in cages beside a seller, while money changers sit at tables with coins and scales.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus finding sellers of oxen, sheep, and doves and seated money changers in the temple, as described in John 2:14 and its Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus raises a whip of cords in a temple courtyard as sheep and oxen run past and money changers recoil beside an overturned table and scattered coins.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 2:15, where Jesus drives sheep and oxen from the temple with a whip made of cords, spills the money changers' coins, and overturns their tables. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward dove sellers in a sunlit temple courtyard as one man lifts a cage of white doves and another looks on.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative portrayal of Jesus telling the dove sellers to take these things away and not make his Father's house a house of trade, informed by the chapter's Berean Interlinear Bible token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands firmly beside an overturned table and scattered coins in a temple courtyard while three disciples watch him, one with a hand on his chest. Doves fly near the table, and people and sheep appear among the pale stone columns.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places the disciples' remembrance of the written words about zeal for God's house in the setting of Jesus clearing the temple. Their gestures and expressions are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone temple courtyard, a man gestures toward Jesus as several others look on. An overturned table and scattered coins lie between them, with animals and sellers in the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 2:18, where the Jewish people ask Jesus what sign He shows them for doing these things. The temple courtyard and overturned table recall the preceding verses; the visual details are imagined. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands among listeners in a sunlit temple courtyard, one hand against his chest and the other raised, with three pools of light on the paving stones.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus answering in the temple. The three pools of light suggest his words about raising the temple in three days; John 2:21 identifies the temple as his body.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A bride and groom hold hands in a sunlit stone courtyard as wedding guests and musicians celebrate. Jesus' mother is imagined as a head-covered woman in blue, with village houses and Galilean hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of the wedding in Cana of Galilee on the third day, with Jesus' mother present, as described in John 2:1. The figures and setting are imagined; the verse's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit temple courtyard, a man holds up three fingers as he speaks to Jesus, while others look on and an ornate stone temple stands behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard conversation reflects John 2:20's question about the temple built over forty-six years and whether Jesus would raise it in three days. The gestures and setting are artistic interpretation, based on the verse and its Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to listeners in a sunlit temple courtyard, with one hand on his chest and the other extended; the Jerusalem temple stands behind him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests John 2:21's meaning: Jesus was speaking about the temple of his body. The verse does not specify this gesture or the arrangement shown.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Five disciples gather around an unlettered scroll in a sunlit garden, with an open rock-hewn tomb and its rolled-away stone behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the disciples recalling Jesus' words and believing Scripture after he was raised from the dead. The garden gathering and scroll are artistic choices, not details specified in John 2:22.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands in a sunlit Jerusalem courtyard among a crowd of people looking toward him; a soft golden glow surrounds his open hand.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 2:23: during the Passover feast in Jerusalem, many believed in Jesus' name as they saw the signs he was doing. The glow is an artistic suggestion; the verse does not identify the signs.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with his hands held together in a sunlit stone courtyard, looking thoughtfully toward a group of attentive people.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests Jesus' discernment and reserve as John 2:24 says He did not entrust Himself to them because He knew all people. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus looks attentively at a seated man while a woman and three other men watch in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 2:25: Jesus needed no one to testify about a person, because he himself knew what was within people.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus and several disciples are welcomed by a man with open arms at a flower-decorated courtyard, where guests gather under a red-and-cream canopy.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus and His disciples being invited to the wedding in John 2:2. The greeting, setting, and appearance of the people are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At a wedding feast, Jesus' mother speaks to him beside an empty earthenware pitcher and cups, while guests gather in a sunlit courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 2:3, when the wine has run out and Jesus' mother tells him that they have no wine. The setting and gestures are artistic details. The source verse uses Nestle 1904 Greek and Berean Interlinear English token glosses; those glosses are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to Mary, who listens with clasped hands, beside clay jars and a small cup at a sunlit wedding gathering.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus speaking to his mother in John 2:4, where he addresses her and says that his hour has not yet come. The gestures and visual details are imagined within the Cana wedding setting. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At a flower-decorated wedding feast, Mary gestures toward Jesus while three servants look on beside large stone jars.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene relates to John 2:5, where Jesus' mother tells the servants to do whatever he says. The appearance of the people and setting is an artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Six large carved stone water jars stand in a sunlit courtyard beside a shallow washing basin and a folded cloth.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 2:6, which describes six stone water jars for the Jewish custom of purification, each with room for two or three metretes. The courtyard, basin, cloth, and decorative details are imagined. The chapter's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward six large stone jars in a sunny wedding courtyard while a servant pours clear water into one; other servants stand beside the water-filled jars.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 2:7: Jesus tells them to fill the jars with water, and they fill them to the brim. The six stone jars come from the preceding verse, John 2:6; the courtyard and figures are artistic interpretation. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures beside large stone jars while a servant lifts a filled cup from one jar and another carries a small vessel toward the seated master of the feast. Guests gather at tables beneath grapevines.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 2:8: Jesus tells them to draw some out and carry it to the master of the feast, and they carry it. The scene's appearance and arrangement are artistic choices. The verse's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At a wedding feast, a man holding a cup of wine gestures toward the bridegroom while two servants stand beside large water jars.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 2:9: after tasting water that had become wine, the master of the feast, unaware of its source, calls the bridegroom, while the servants who drew the water know. The setting, appearances, gestures, and moment are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two disciples in robes walk together along a sunlit stone path toward a village of simple homes, surrounded by trees and wildflowers.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the disciples going away again to their homes in John 20:10. The people and setting are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mary weeps and bends toward the dark entrance of a rock-cut tomb, surrounded by sunlit stones and flowers.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:11, where Mary weeps outside the tomb and stoops to look into it.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman looks toward two white-clad angels seated at opposite ends of an empty stone burial place, in a warmly lit chamber.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 20:12: she sees two angels in white, sitting at the head and feet of the place where Jesus' body had lain.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A tearful woman gestures as she speaks with two attentive men beside a stone opening, surrounded by flowers in warm light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the exchange in John 20:13: a woman is asked why she weeps and says her Lord has been taken away and she does not know where he has been laid. The setting and figures' appearance are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman turns with a questioning expression toward Jesus, who stands nearby, in a sunlit garden beside a stone opening.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 20:14: after speaking, the woman turns and sees Jesus standing there without knowing that it is him. The garden and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A tearful woman gestures toward Jesus in a flower-filled garden as he looks at her; a stone opening stands behind him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:15: Jesus speaks to the weeping woman, who supposes him to be the gardener and asks where the one she seeks has been laid. The garden details and poses are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mary turns toward Jesus with an expression of joyful recognition as he reaches toward her in a sunlit garden beside a rock-cut tomb.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:16, in which Jesus says Mary’s name and she turns and addresses him as Rabboni, meaning Teacher. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a flowering garden, Jesus stands speaking to a kneeling woman, holding one hand up as she reaches toward him and extending the other toward a path.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene reflecting Jesus' words to the woman in John 20:17: he tells her not to touch him and sends her to tell his brothers that he is ascending to his Father and their Father, his God and their God. The setting and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mary Magdalene speaks with open hands to a group of attentive disciples in a sunlit stone room.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 20:18, in which Mary Magdalene brings the disciples word that she has seen the Lord and tells them what He said to her.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open hands among startled disciples in a lamplit room, with a closed wooden door behind them and evening visible through a window.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:19: on the evening of the first day of the week, Jesus stands among the disciples behind shut doors and speaks peace to them. The room, appearances, and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Mary Magdalene approaches a rock-cut tomb at predawn and looks toward its open entrance; a large stone stands beside it among rocks and flowers.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 20:1: Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb early while it is still dark and sees the stone removed. The setting and appearance are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus shows his marked hands and side to joyful disciples gathered around him in a warmly lit room.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:20, in which the Lord shows the disciples his hands and side and they rejoice at seeing him. The room, clothing, and individual expressions are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to a group gathered in a stone room, with a sunlit path visible through the doorway.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus offering peace and sending those he addresses, as the Father sent him. The room, gestures, and path are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus breathes toward a group of attentive disciples gathered in a warmly lit room; delicate pale lines suggest his breath.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:22, where Jesus breathes on them and tells them to receive the Holy Spirit. The room, figures and visible breath are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to attentive listeners in a warmly lit room, with a loose cord and a tied cord on a table in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses loose and tied cords to suggest the verse's contrast between sins forgiven and sins retained; the setting and objects are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands among disciples in a warmly lit room while Thomas walks apart along the street outside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene reflecting John 20:24: Thomas, called Didymus, was not with the others when Jesus came. The setting and figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warmly lit room, four disciples speak earnestly to a seated man, who points to his palm as he listens and responds.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:25: the other disciples say they have seen the Lord, and the listener describes the evidence he says he must see and touch before he will believe. The room and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open arms among his attentive disciples in a warmly lit room, with a closed wooden door behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:26: eight days later the disciples, including Thomas, are inside when Jesus stands among them despite the closed doors and greets them with peace. The setting and appearances are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus extends a wounded hand toward Thomas and opens his robe to reveal a small wound at his side; Thomas reaches toward him in a warmly lit room.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus inviting Thomas to see his hands and bring his hand to his side, and calling him to believe, in John 20:27. The room, appearance, and gestures are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Thomas kneels and speaks with open hands toward Jesus, who stands facing him in a warmly lit stone room.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:28, where Thomas answers and addresses him as his Lord and his God. The setting and gestures are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures gently while speaking with an attentive man in a warmly lit room, with sunlight entering through an open doorway.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative setting for Jesus speaking about seeing and believing and the blessing of those who believe without seeing. The room and gestures are artistic choices, not details specified by John 20:29.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A distressed woman gestures urgently as she speaks to two concerned disciples on a stone path; an open rock-cut tomb and a village appear behind them in the morning light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 20:2, showing the woman telling Simon Peter and the other disciple that the Lord has been taken from the tomb and that they do not know where he has been laid. The setting and appearance of the people are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus takes the hand of a seated man on a rocky path while three disciples watch, with a lake and hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene suggesting one of the many other signs Jesus performed before his disciples that John 20:30 says are not written in this book; the verse does not describe this particular event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group gathers around a blank scroll in a sunlit courtyard, looking toward Jesus as he opens his arms in a flowering garden.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects the verse's purpose: the written testimony invites belief that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and life in his name. The gathering is not an event narrated by the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two disciples hurry along a sunlit garden path toward a rock-cut tomb, surrounded by flowers, trees, and hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:3, in which Peter and the other disciple go toward the tomb. The setting and their appearance are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men run along a rocky path toward a rock-cut tomb; the leading disciple reaches its entrance while Peter follows behind.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene based on John 20:4, where the two run together and the other disciple runs ahead of Peter and reaches the tomb first.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man bends outside a rock-cut tomb and looks at pale linen cloths lying on a stone surface inside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:5: he stoops and sees the linen cloths lying there, but does not enter. The setting and appearance are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Simon Peter looks at pale linen cloths lying on a stone resting place inside a rock-hewn tomb, while another man stands at the entrance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:6, in which Simon Peter enters the tomb and sees the linen cloths lying there. The setting, appearances, and arrangement are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit rock-hewn tomb, a folded ivory cloth rests alone on a stone ledge, separated from loose linen cloths nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:7, showing the cloth that had been on His head folded separately from the linen cloths. The tomb setting and light are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A disciple pauses inside a sunlit rock-hewn tomb, looking with wonder at a stone burial place draped with pale linen.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 20:8: the other disciple enters the tomb, sees, and believes. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two thoughtful men stand beside an open rock-cut tomb at dawn, one holding an unlettered scroll; folded linen rests inside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes their not yet understanding the Scripture that he must rise from the dead. The figures, scroll, tomb setting, and gestures are artistic interpretation rather than details stated in this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward three fishermen carrying freshly caught fish in a net and basket beside a boat on a sunlit lakeshore.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:10, where Jesus asks them to bring some of the fish they have just caught; the setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Simon Peter and other fishermen draw a full, unbroken net of large fish onto a rocky lakeshore in golden light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 21:11, where Simon Peter draws an untorn net containing 153 large fish to land. The setting and other fishermen are artistic details; the illustration does not establish a count.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus extends his hands toward disciples gathered around a breakfast of bread and fish beside a lake in the morning light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus inviting the disciples to breakfast and their quiet recognition of him as Lord in John 21:12. The setting and visual details are an artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus offers a round loaf to a seated man while holding a basket of bread and fish, surrounded by men beside a lake.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:13, in which Jesus takes bread and gives it to them, and likewise the fish. The lakeside setting and visual details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open hands among disciples gathered beneath a tree, with a lake and boats in the sunlit background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the risen Jesus revealed to his disciples, reflecting John 21:14, which identifies this as the third time. The landscape and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with Simon Peter beside the remains of a meal, while lambs rest nearby in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 21:15: after they had dined, Jesus asks Peter about his love and tells him to feed his lambs. The lambs pictured express that charge and are not stated to be physically present in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward sheep while speaking with Simon, who holds a hand to his chest, in a sunlit pastoral landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus asking Simon about his love and telling him to shepherd his sheep; the flock gives the command a visual form, not a claim that sheep were present.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks gently to a sorrowful Peter, who kneels with one hand over his heart, while sheep graze in a sunlit landscape beside the water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes Jesus asking Peter a third time about his love, Peter's grief and response, and Jesus' charge to feed his sheep. The grazing sheep and setting are artistic choices, not details asserted by this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: An older man stretches out his hands as another man holds his sash and guides him along a rocky path above a lakeside town.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects the verse's contrast between the freedom of youth and old age, when another will dress and lead the person where he does not wish to go.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures invitingly as a solemn disciple walks beside him on a rocky path above a sunlit lake, with hills and a village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus inviting a disciple to follow him, reflecting the verse’s words about the death by which he would glorify God. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with an open hand on a rocky lakeshore as disciples look toward him beside a boat and fishing nets, with blue water and hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus revealing himself again to his disciples at the Sea of Tiberias in John 21:1. The setting, poses, number of disciples, and visual details are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Peter turns to look at a disciple following him as Jesus walks ahead along a sunlit path.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Peter turning to see the disciple whom Jesus loved following. John 21:20 also recalls that this disciple had reclined against Jesus at supper and asked who was betraying him.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Peter sits beside Jesus beneath a tree, gesturing toward a man standing nearby with a fishing net in a sunlit lakeside landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of Peter seeing a man and asking Jesus what about him in John 21:21. The setting, appearance and identity of the other man are artistic choices not specified in this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to a man walking beside him on a sunlit path, while another man stands farther back near the water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene evoking Jesus' call to follow him and his conditional words about another man remaining until he comes; the landscape and details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man gestures as he speaks to three attentive companions in a sunlit stone courtyard, while a younger disciple stands nearby beneath the trees.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the saying spreading among the brothers in John 21:23. The verse clarifies that Jesus spoke conditionally about the disciple remaining until he comes, rather than saying that the disciple would not die.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-haired disciple holds a reed pen over a blank scroll while two companions listen beside him in a sunlit room overlooking a distant blue landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene represents the disciple who bears witness and wrote these things, and the shared confidence that his testimony is true; the setting and companions are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: An ancient writer pauses at a low desk as uncountable blank scrolls spread across the sunlit hills toward the horizon.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual metaphor for John 21:25: the many other things Jesus did are suggested by more scrolls than the landscape can hold. The writer, setting and arrangement are artistic choices, not a claimed eyewitness portrait or additional event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Seven men gather in conversation beneath a tree near the water, with boats and distant hills behind them, in a warm watercolor illustration.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the seven disciples together in John 21:2; their appearances, conversation and surroundings are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At night, five men in a wooden fishing boat draw up an empty net by lamplight, with a moonlit shoreline in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:3, when Simon Peter and his companions go fishing and catch nothing that night.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At sunrise, Jesus stands on a rocky shore facing disciples in a wooden boat; they look toward him with questioning expressions. Fish rest over a small fire in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:4: morning has come, Jesus stands on the shore, and the disciples do not yet know it is him. The boat, landscape and foreground details are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks from a lakeshore to fishermen in a wooden boat; one holds out an empty basket as the others look toward him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:5, where Jesus asks whether they have any fish and they answer no. The lakeside setting, boat, clothing and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Fishermen in a wooden boat strain to pull a net crowded with fish from the water beside them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:6: after the instruction to cast the net on the boat's right side, the catch is so large that they cannot haul it in.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Peter, wearing a secured outer garment, splashes into the sea beside a wooden boat as a disciple points toward Jesus on the distant shore.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:7: the disciple whom Jesus loved identifies the Lord to Peter, who puts on his outer garment and casts himself into the sea. The setting and visual details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several disciples in a wooden fishing boat pull a fish-filled net through the water near a sunny shore.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 21:8: the other disciples come in the boat near land, dragging the net of fish. The setting and appearances are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: People step onto a rocky lakeshore and look toward fish resting on glowing coals, with bread nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 21:9: those coming onto land see a fire of coals with fish on it and bread. The setting and figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand toward Nicodemus, who listens with his hand at his chin, beside an oil lamp on a stone terrace at night.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 3:10: Jesus answers Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, asking why he does not know these things. The nighttime setting draws on John 3:2; the terrace, lamp, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a lamplit stone courtyard at night, Jesus in a pale robe speaks with open hands to an older, contemplative Nicodemus in a dark robe; a city glows beneath the stars behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative nighttime conversation between Jesus and Nicodemus evokes John 3:11: Jesus speaks of knowing, seeing, and bearing witness, and of that testimony not being received. The particular place and gestures are imagined; the verse addresses its listeners with a plural 'you'.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on a stone terrace at night, speaking to Nicodemus by lamplight while gesturing toward the ground and pointing toward the starry sky above the city.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays Jesus speaking with Nicodemus at night and uses his gestures and the sky to suggest his question in John 3:12 about believing earthly and heavenly things. The setting and gestures are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed man representing the Son of Man descends amid glowing clouds above a sunlit hillside, olive trees, distant mountains, and a village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 3:13 says no one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man. This scene imaginatively depicts his coming down; its visible details are not described in the verse. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Moses raises a pole bearing a bronze-colored serpent while people look upward in the wilderness; Jesus appears on a cross on a distant sunlit hill.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative pairing brings events from different times into one landscape, evoking John 3:14's comparison between Moses lifting the serpent in the wilderness and the Son of Man being lifted up.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a leafy tree, with an arm around a child, and gestures to adults and children gathered around Him. A stream, flowers, hills, and a village fill the sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene responds to John 3:15's Berean Interlinear glosses: people look toward Jesus in trust, while the flowing stream and flourishing tree suggest the eternal life promised to everyone believing in Him. It does not depict a recorded historical event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open hands before men, women, and children in a sunlit landscape, with a stream and a wooden cross on a distant hill.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative meditation on John 3:16. The people look toward the Son whom God gave in love for the world; the cross and flourishing landscape suggest that gift and the promise of eternal life to everyone who believes in Him. The verse does not describe this particular scene. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches down to help a weary man rise on a rocky path while adults and children watch, with a sunlit village and hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 3:17: the Son's compassionate help suggests God sending Him into the world so that the world might be saved through Him, rather than to judge it. The scene is not an event narrated in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus extends his hands toward a man approaching him, while another man looks down in a shaded archway beside a hanging balance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 3:18: the person facing Jesus suggests the one believing in the only begotten Son, who is not judged; the person turned away and the balance evoke the one who has not believed and is already judged. The courtyard and figures are artistic interpretation, not events described in the verse. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are uncurated, not GBT-approved.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a man clutching a small pouch and a woman gathering her shawl move toward a dark archway, with an open gate, plants, and baskets behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays John 3:19's contrast between the light that came into the world and people choosing darkness because of evil deeds. The figures and setting are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A thoughtful bearded man in richly colored robes sits between two elders in a sunlit stone courtyard, listening as they speak; a city and an olive tree appear behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 3:1 introduces Nicodemus as a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews. This courtyard conversation is an imaginative illustration of his role, not an event described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in a shaded stone room gathers coins into his cloak beside an open wooden chest, while sunlight streams through an open doorway.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Inspired by the Berean Interlinear word glosses for John 3:20, this imagined scene depicts someone concealing wrongdoing in the shadows to illustrate the verse's warning that those who practice evil avoid the light lest their works be exposed. The specific incident is not described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling artisan in an apron presents a mended clay jar to a woman outside a shaded workshop, with golden sunlight filling a stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene uses a repaired vessel brought into the light to suggest John 3:21: the one practicing truth comes to the light so that works done in God may be seen.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits with several disciples beneath a tree beside a stream, while a disciple supports a man being baptized in the water; golden hills and a village lie beyond them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 3:22, where Jesus stays with His disciples in Judea and baptizing takes place. John 4:2 clarifies that His disciples carried out the baptisms.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist stands in clear water, baptizing a man as people approach along a sunlit bank.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John baptizing at Aenon near Salim, where John 3:23 describes abundant water and people coming to be baptized. The landscape, figures and moment are artistic interpretations; the verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John, wearing a rough brown garment, speaks to a group of listeners beside a river in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 3:24 says John had not yet been cast into prison. This riverside gathering is an imaginative depiction of that time.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men in robes sit beside a river and gesture as they speak with a fourth man. A bowl of water rests in front of them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 3:25 describes a debate between John's disciples and a Jewish man about purification. The riverside setting, gestures, and bowl are imaginative details. The English word glosses consulted are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist in a rough brown garment listens to three men beside a river, while people gather and a person is helped into the water in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 3:26, in which people tell John that the one to whom he bore witness is baptizing and that all are coming to him. The appearance and arrangement of the people and river are artistic interpretation. The verse's English token glosses are from the uncurated Berean Interlinear, not a GBT-approved translation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist gestures toward rays of sunlight while speaking with two listeners beside a river; one listener holds his hands open.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative riverside conversation uses sunlight and open hands to suggest John 3:27's teaching that a person can receive nothing unless it has been given from heaven. The verse does not describe these gestures or the scene.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist speaks to listeners beside a river, touching his chest and gesturing toward a distant road.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John telling his listeners that he is not the Christ but was sent ahead of Him. The riverbank, gestures, and empty road are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling bride holding a bouquet stands beside a speaking bridegroom beneath a flowered canopy. Nearby, his friend listens with a joyful smile and his hands clasped to his chest in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative wedding scene illustrates the bridegroom and bride and the friend whose joy is fulfilled as he listens to the bridegroom's voice in John 3:29.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a lamplit stone courtyard at night, an older man in a striped head covering gestures with open hands as he speaks to Jesus, who sits facing him. The moon and distant buildings appear beyond them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 3:2: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night and speaks to him as a teacher from God, acknowledging that Jesus' signs show God is with him. Nicodemus is identified in John 3:1; the courtyard, lamp, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits by a sunlit river, speaking to a group gathered around Him, while John the Baptist smiles and gestures toward Him from the side.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows John gladly directing attention to Jesus, illustrating John's words that Jesus must increase while he must decrease. The particular setting and encounter are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit rocky landscape, a man gestures as he speaks to a seated listener while a robed figure stands on a hillside beneath rays of light.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 3:31: the figure in the light represents the One from heaven who is above all, while the man on the earth speaks from the earth. The people, setting, and gestures are artistic choices, not a historical scene described by the verse. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures while speaking in a sunlit village street as people nearby turn away or walk on.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 3:32: he testifies to what he has seen and heard, yet no one receives his testimony. The village, people, and moment are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man presses a seal onto a rolled parchment while another man speaks beside him, at a wooden table in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the sealing of a scroll to evoke the person who receives His testimony and affirms that God is true. The verse does not describe a literal scroll or sealing ceremony.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree and speaks to a small group of listeners in a sunlit Judean landscape, while a white dove and golden rays fill the sky above them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering reflects John 3:34's words about the one God sent speaking God's words and the Spirit being given without measure. The dove and expansive light are visual symbols, not a depiction of an event described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands on a hillside above a lake and a distant town, holding a luminous globe in his open hand and looking toward golden light from the sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual metaphor for John 3:35: the light suggests the Father's love for the Son, and the globe in Jesus's hand symbolizes all things given into his hand. The verse does not describe this visible scene.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a listener under a leafy tree by a flowing spring, while another man walks away beneath a dark raincloud in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses a living tree and flowing water to suggest the eternal life possessed by the one who believes in the Son. The lingering storm over the man turning away suggests that the one who does not obey the Son will not see life and that God's wrath remains on him. The encounter is imagined, based on John 3:36 and its Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he speaks to Nicodemus in a courtyard at night, with an oil lamp and a small green seedling in a clay pot between them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined nighttime conversation illustrates Jesus telling Nicodemus that anyone must be born from above to see the kingdom of God. The seedling is a visual metaphor, not a detail stated in the passage.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: An older, grey-bearded Nicodemus gestures with open hands as Jesus listens beside an oil lamp, with a moonlit city beyond the stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Nicodemus asking Jesus how someone can be born when old and whether a person can enter his mother's womb a second time and be born. The courtyard and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a moonlit stone courtyard, Jesus gestures as he speaks with Nicodemus beside an oil lamp and a bowl of water; an open gate leads toward a garden and distant buildings.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects Jesus' words to Nicodemus in John 3:5 about being born of water and the Spirit and entering the kingdom of God. The water vessel, olive foliage, open gate, setting, and appearances are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit courtyard, a seated mother cradles her swaddled newborn while a man lifts his hands and face toward the sky, his shawl and nearby olive leaves stirred by a breeze.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pairs human birth with a wind-stirred, receptive figure to reflect John 3:6's contrast between what is born of flesh and what is born of the Spirit; it does not depict the Spirit literally.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to Nicodemus in a moonlit stone courtyard; Nicodemus listens with his hand on his chin, and a small green plant grows in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places Jesus and Nicodemus in their nighttime conversation. The young plant symbolizes the new life from above of which Jesus speaks in John 3:7; the plant is an artistic addition.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man sits beneath an olive tree on a sunlit hillside, listening as wind lifts his robe and carries leaves over the grass.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 3:8's comparison: the wind is heard though its origin and destination are unknown, and so it is with everyone born of the Spirit. The English word glosses consulted are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Nicodemus gestures as he speaks to Jesus across a low table lit by an oil lamp; both sit in a stone room open to the moonlit night.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Nicodemus asking Jesus how these things can be in John 3:9. The nighttime conversation draws on John 3:2; the room, appearances, clothing, and gestures are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not Global Bible Tools-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on the edge of a stone well and speaks with an open hand to a Samaritan woman standing beside a large clay water jar. Water glints in the well, with trees, hills, and a village in the sunlit distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 4:10, where Jesus speaks of the gift of God and says that the woman would have asked him and he would have given her living water. The visible water and setting are artistic choices. The source verse's English token glosses are Berean Interlinear glosses marked uncurated, not GBT-approved.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures toward a deep stone well as she speaks to Jesus, who sits beside it with empty hands; an earthen jar rests near her.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined moment inspired by John 4:11: the woman asks Jesus where He has living water when He has nothing to draw with and the well is deep. The word glosses used to guide the scene are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, as identified in the reader's source note.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman holding a clay jar gestures toward Jesus, who sits beside a stone well. Sheep and a cow drink at a trough behind them in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of the Samaritan woman asking Jesus whether he is greater than Jacob, who gave the well and from which he, his sons, and his livestock drank. The animals evoke her reference; the verse does not say they were present during the conversation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he speaks to the Samaritan woman beside a stone well; a clay water jar and cup sit nearby in a sunlit, dry landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well as he says that everyone who drinks this water will thirst again. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation; the token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a woman seated beside a stone well, her clay water jar nearby, while a ribbon of water and flowering greenery rises from her chest into the sunlit air.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene visualizes Jesus' promise that the water he gives becomes a spring within the recipient, welling up to eternal life. The visible spring and flowers are an artistic metaphor, not a visible event described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman extends her open hands toward Jesus, who sits beside a round stone well. A clay water jar and rope rest nearby in a sunlit, hilly landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates the woman asking Jesus for water so that she will not thirst or need to come here to draw, in John 4:15. The appearance, gestures, and landscape are artistic interpretation. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and gestures toward a distant village while the Samaritan woman stands beside a clay water jar and listens.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the conversation at the well as Jesus tells the woman to go, call her husband, and come here, following the verse's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman stands beside a clay jar with one hand on her chest, speaking with Jesus, who sits by a stone well and gestures gently. Sunlit hills and a distant village fill the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:17, where the woman answers that she has no husband and Jesus says she has spoken correctly. The setting, expressions, and gestures are artistic choices; the verse relationship follows the Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, speaking with a woman holding a clay water jar. Five pebbles together and one apart rest on the well in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes Jesus' conversation with the Samaritan woman in John 4:18, where he acknowledges that she has spoken truthfully and speaks of her five past husbands and the man who is not her husband now. The pebbles are an artistic addition suggesting those relationships.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures as she speaks to Jesus, who sits beside a stone well. A clay water jar rests nearby, with a leafy tree, sunlit hills and a village around them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 4:19, in which the woman tells Jesus she understands him to be a prophet. The well comes from the surrounding passage; the lesson identifies its English token glosses as Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree listening to a gesturing follower. Behind them, robed Pharisees converse while a disciple baptizes a person in the river and others gather nearby; golden hills and a village rise in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 4:1, in which Jesus learns that the Pharisees have heard he is making and baptizing more disciples than John. The setting and conversations are imagined; the disciple performing the baptism reflects the clarification in John 4:2.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures toward a mountain while speaking with Jesus beside a stone well; a water jar and a winding road sit among sunlit hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the conversation in John 4:20, where the woman contrasts her ancestors' worship on the mountain with the claim that Jerusalem is the place to worship. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a sunlit mountain while speaking with a woman beside a stone well; her clay water jar rests at her feet.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman as he tells her that a time is coming when worship of the Father will be neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. The setting and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, speaking with an open hand to a Samaritan woman seated near a clay water jar, with sunlit hills and olive trees behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well. In John 4:22 he contrasts worship of what is not known with worship of what is known and says that salvation is from the Jews. The chapter's word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor illustration of Jesus seated by a stone well speaking with a Samaritan woman beside a clay jar, with people praying in the sunlit fields beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well. The distant worshipers are an artistic addition illustrating John 4:23, where Jesus speaks of true worshipers worshiping the Father in spirit and truth and says that the Father seeks such worshipers.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, one hand over his heart and the other raised toward the sky, while a Samaritan woman listens beside a clay water jar. A sunlit village and hills lie in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places Jesus and the Samaritan woman at the well as he teaches that God is Spirit and that worship must be in spirit and truth. The gestures and setting interpret the teaching rather than depicting details stated in this verse. The chapter's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures toward Jesus beside a stone well, with a clay water jar in the foreground and sunlit hills and a village behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:25, where the woman speaks of the coming Messiah, called Christ, who will tell them all things. The appearance and details of the scene are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits at a stone well and gestures as he speaks to a Samaritan woman beside her clay water jar, with sunlit trees and hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:26 and its setting at Jacob's well: Jesus speaks to the Samaritan woman after she mentions the coming Messiah. The source identifies the English word glosses as Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and speaks with a woman next to a clay water jar, while four arriving disciples look on in surprise in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:27: Jesus speaks with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well as his disciples arrive, amazed but not voicing the questions mentioned in the verse. The scene is informed by the Berean Interlinear token glosses; the appearances and setting details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures while speaking to two men near a stone town gate; a clay water pot stands unattended beside a well behind her.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of John 4:28: the woman leaves her water pot, goes into the city, and speaks to the men. The setting, appearance, and gestures are artistic interpretation. The word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear Bible and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures to attentive townspeople in a sunlit stone village, inviting them toward a man seated beside a distant well.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows the Samaritan woman inviting the townspeople to see the man who told her what she had done and asking whether he could be the Christ, as in John 4:29. The appearances, setting, and gestures are imagined. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands on a riverbank while two disciples baptize a man and a woman in the water, with hills and a village beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative riverside scene illustrating John 4:2: Jesus himself did not baptize; his disciples did. The setting and the participants' appearances are imagined. The chapter identifies its English word glosses as Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Townspeople walk out of a stone city along a sunlit path toward Jesus, who sits beside a well under a tree.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:30, in which people go out of the city and come to Jesus; the figures and setting are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well while a disciple offers him bread and other disciples gather around beneath a tree.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the disciples asking Jesus, their Rabbi, to eat in John 4:31. The bread, gestures and visual details are imagined; the well follows the surrounding passage. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and gestures as he speaks to four disciples. One holds a basket of bread, while the others listen beneath a leafy tree in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts Jesus telling his disciples that he has food to eat which they do not know, as reflected in the Berean Interlinear token glosses. The offered bread evokes their earlier invitation to eat; the food he speaks of is left unpictured.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well as four disciples turn toward one another with puzzled expressions and questioning gestures. Trees, fields, hills, and a distant village fill the sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 4:33, where the disciples ask one another whether someone brought Jesus anything to eat. The well comes from the surrounding passage; the figures' appearances and gestures are imagined. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to attentive disciples beside a stone well. One holds a basket of bread as villagers approach from a sunlit town.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 4:34, where Jesus describes His food as doing the will of the One who sent Him and finishing His work. The bread and approaching villagers suggest the surrounding story; their appearance and arrangement are imagined. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a sunlit field of pale ripe grain while a group of listeners gathers around him, with hills and a village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene draws on John 4:35 and its Berean Interlinear token glosses: Jesus asks his listeners to lift their eyes and see fields already white for harvest. The setting and figures are an artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two smiling field workers in robes face each other in a golden field. One scatters seed, while the other carries a basket and armful of grain, with a small pouch at his belt.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene echoes the harvest metaphor in John 4:36: the sower and reaper rejoice together, while the reaper gathers the harvest and a small pouch suggests the reward. The abundant field and warm light allude to fruit for eternal life.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit countryside, one farmer scatters seeds over dark tilled soil while another cuts ripe golden grain with a sickle.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of the saying in John 4:37: one person sows and another reaps.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a golden wheat field as disciples look on; reapers cut and gather grain while other workers labor among sheaves in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus sending his followers to reap where others have already labored, as described in John 4:38.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures as she speaks to attentive townspeople outside a sunlit stone city, while Jesus sits by a stone well in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 4:39, where many Samaritans believe in Jesus because of the woman's testimony that he told her all she had done. The setting and gestures are artistic interpretation. The verse's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a winding country path away from a stone settlement, with hills and water in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' journey: John 4:3 says he left Judea and went again into Galilee. The setting and details are artistic interpretation. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks with smiling Samaritan villagers as a man gestures toward the open doorway of a stone home, with hills and village houses beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative welcome illustrates the Samaritans asking Jesus to stay with them in John 4:40. The verse says he stayed there two days; this single scene does not depict the duration.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he speaks to a gathering of Samaritan villagers beneath a leafy tree, while more people approach along a path between sunlit stone houses.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Samaritan villagers hearing Jesus in the setting of John 4:41, where many more believed because of his word; the English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone village courtyard, Samaritan townspeople speak animatedly with a woman in a head covering, while a seated man gestures toward Jesus standing beside them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 4:42, where the Samaritans tell the woman that they have heard for themselves and know Jesus is truly the Savior of the world. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.
