records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, wearing light robes, walks along a sunlit path away from a village, with people behind him and fields, hills, and a lake in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 4:43 says that after two days he departed from there for Galilee; the preceding passage places him among the Samaritans. This scene imagines the village, figures, and journey.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures while speaking to three men beneath a tree near a sunlit hillside village; a woman with a jar and a man working attend to their tasks beside the stone houses.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus’ testimony that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. The setting, companions, and townspeople’s actions are artistic interpretations, not details stated in John 4:44.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, wearing a cream tunic and reddish-brown mantle, is warmly greeted by Galilean men and women on a sunlit stone path. Olive branches, village houses, hills, and a glimpse of water fill the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined welcome in Galilee illustrates John 4:45: the Galileans received Jesus after seeing what he had done in Jerusalem during the feast, which they themselves had attended. The meeting and its setting are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A concerned royal official sits beside his sick son, resting a hand on the boy's head as he lies in bed. A lakeside village is visible through the window.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the royal official and his sick son in Capernaum mentioned in John 4:46. The verse also says Jesus returned to Cana of Galilee, where he had made water into wine.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus listens as a worried man in ornate blue robes gestures down a sunlit village road, with a lake and hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:47: a royal official asks Jesus to come down and heal his son, who is near death. The setting and gestures are imagined; the son is not shown.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to a richly dressed royal official while several people listen in a sunlit village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Jesus speaking to the royal official in John 4:48 about seeing signs and wonders and believing. The listeners, setting, and appearances are imagined. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, keyed to the Nestle 1904 Greek text by biblicalhumanities.org; they are not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A richly dressed royal official kneels with outstretched hands as Jesus listens beneath a tree; a winding road crosses the sunlit hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:49, in which the royal official asks Jesus to come down before his child dies. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a rocky path through sunlit hills, with olive trees, stone terraces, and a village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus passing through Samaria in John 4:4. The landscape and visual details are artistic interpretation. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit village road, Jesus extends his hand toward a man who looks back at him while walking away with a staff and a bundle.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 4:50: Jesus tells the man to go because his son lives; the man believes Jesus' word and goes on his way. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two servants meet a robed father on a sunlit road; one gestures as the father listens, with hills, trees, and a distant village behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined meeting based on John 4:51 and the Berean Interlinear word glosses: as the father goes down, his servants meet him with the news that his boy lives. The setting, clothing, and expressions are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit road above a lake, a richly robed father listens as a servant gestures while two other servants stand nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene shows the father asking his servants when his son began to get better. In John 4:52, they answer that the fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour. The landscape and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded father holds his smiling son's hand at his bedside, looking upward as five members of the household gather in a warm, sunlit home.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:53: the father recognized that the hour matched Jesus' words that his son lived, and he and his whole household believed. The home, gathering, gestures, and appearances are artistic choices. The English token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, in a white robe and red cloak, speaks to a richly dressed royal official on a sunlit stone path in a Galilean village, with blue water and hills in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene recalls Jesus reassuring the royal official in Cana. John 4:54 identifies the healing of the official's son at a distance as Jesus' second sign after coming from Judea to Galilee.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks toward a stone town beside a cultivated field bordered by low stone walls and olive trees, with sunlit hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:5: Jesus comes to Sychar in Samaria near the plot of ground Jacob gave his son Joseph. The town and landscape are artistic interpretations. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus rests wearily on the edge of a stone well, his head in his hand, as a sunlit path winds through fields and hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:6: Jesus, weary from his journey, sits at Jacob's well about the sixth hour. His appearance and the well and landscape are artistic interpretation. The scene follows the verse and its Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman holding a clay jar stands beside a stone well and looks toward Jesus, who is seated and gestures to her. A rope hangs from a wooden crossbeam, with trees, hills, and a village in the sunlit background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:7, where a woman from Samaria comes to draw water and Jesus asks her for a drink. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group of robed travelers in a sunlit stone-town market, one offering coins to a seller holding flatbreads, with baskets of fruit and other food on the stall.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' disciples in the city to buy food, as John 4:8 describes. The market, people, and exchange are artistic details; the verse's token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures in surprise toward Jesus, who sits beside a stone well; her clay water jar stands at her side in a sunny landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:9: the Samaritan woman questions Jesus about his request for a drink, and the verse notes that Jews did not associate with Samaritans. The setting and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone street, a man holds a rolled woven mat while three men face him and two gesture toward him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 5:10, where Jewish people tell the man who had been healed that it is the Sabbath and he may not take up his mat. The setting, appearance, and gestures are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man carrying a rolled mat gestures as he speaks with two listeners on a sunlit stone walkway beside a pool.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the healed man answering that the one who made him well told him to take up his mat and walk, as in John 5:11. The setting and appearances are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men question a man holding a rolled sleeping mat on a sunlit stone street; one gestures with open hands as the man looks uncertain.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the question in John 5:12. The rolled mat draws on John 5:11. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man holding a rolled mat stands beside a pool under sunlit stone columns, looking toward a crowd in which a robed figure walks away.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 5:13: the man who had been healed did not know who Jesus was, and Jesus had moved away while a crowd was there. The setting and poses are interpretive; the verse relationship follows the chapter's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit temple court, Jesus rests a hand on a man's shoulder and gestures as the man listens, holding a rolled woven mat.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 5:14, where Jesus finds the man made well in the temple and warns him to sin no more so that nothing worse may happen. The mat recalls the earlier account; its presence at this meeting is imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling man holding a rolled mat speaks to two listeners and gestures toward Jesus walking down a sunlit stone street.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the man telling the Jews that Jesus had made him well. The street, gestures, listeners, and Jesus appearing in the distance are artistic choices rather than details specified in John 5:15.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands beside a stone colonnade facing several men who gesture toward him, while another man carries a rolled mat beside the pool.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined confrontation illustrates John 5:16's account of Jews persecuting Jesus because he was doing these things on the Sabbath. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing in the preceding passage.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among attentive listeners and gestures as he speaks in a sunlit stone colonnade. Behind them, a man carries a rolled mat beside a pool.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus answering his listeners, reflecting John 5:17's statement that his Father is working until now and that he too is working. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing earlier in John 5; the setting, gestures and arrangement are imagined. The verse's token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures upward in a sunlit stone courtyard while several men confer tensely nearby; a man behind him carries a rolled mat.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene relates to John 5:18, where the Jews seek all the more to kill Jesus because he was breaking the Sabbath and called God his own Father, making himself equal with God. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing in the surrounding passage; the setting and gestures are imagined. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, speaking to listeners and raising one hand toward the sky, while a smiling man stands nearby carrying a rolled mat.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene represents Jesus explaining that the Son does what he sees the Father doing. The man with the mat recalls the earlier healing in John 5; the verse does not describe these visual details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus in a cream robe and brown shawl walks up a rocky path toward Jerusalem's sunlit walls. Other travelers and a donkey approach the city, where crowds gather beneath colorful cloths near the gate.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of Jesus going up to Jerusalem when a Jewish feast was taking place, as described in John 5:1. The feast is unnamed; the travelers, decorations, cityscape, and figures' appearances are artistic additions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus looks and gestures toward sunlight beside a man holding a rolled mat, while onlookers watch in wonder by a pool with stone colonnades.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene reflects John 5:20: the light suggests the Father's love for the Son and the works He shows Him, while the onlookers and distant brightness evoke the greater works to come and the wonder they will inspire. The man with the mat and the pool recall the earlier healing in John 5; this particular scene is not described as an event in verse 20. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches for the hand of a man rising from a stone tomb, wrapped in burial cloth, amid flowers on a sunlit hillside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual meditation on John 5:21: the Father raises the dead and gives life, and the Son gives life to whom he wills. The image does not depict a specific event narrated in this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on a stone seat holding bronze balance scales in a beam of golden light as people watch nearby, with olive trees and a hillside village in the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 5:22: the scales and heavenly light suggest the Father's gift of all judgment to the Son. The scene is an artistic illustration, not an event described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures to an attentive group in a sunlit stone courtyard while one man turns away at the edge.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene reflects John 5:23's teaching that honoring the Son is inseparable from honoring the Father who sent him; the sunlight is symbolic, not a literal depiction of the Father.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a listener stepping from barren, stony ground toward a sunlit path lined with flowers.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests John 5:24 through a change from barren ground to a flowering path. The verse says that the one who hears Jesus' word and believes the One who sent Him has eternal life, does not come into judgment, and has passed out of death into life. Its English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches toward people rising among rocks and wildflowers near a stone tomb, with a sunlit landscape behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of Jesus' words that the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. The awakening figures are a visual metaphor, not an event narrated in this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands in a flower-filled garden on a Judean hillside, one hand over his glowing chest and the other extended toward a green sapling beneath a sunlit sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the Son's inner light and the light of the sky as a visual metaphor for John 5:26: as the Father has life in Himself, He has given the Son to have life in Himself.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on a raised stone seat holding balanced scales as people gather around him in a sunlit courtyard, with olive trees and hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses scales and light from the sky to suggest the authority the Father gives the Son of Man to execute judgment in John 5:27. The setting, people and visual symbols are artistic inventions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward men and women listening from open stone tombs in a sunlit hillside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the coming hour in John 5:28, when all those in the tombs will hear his voice. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The verse's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: People emerge from rock-hewn tombs; some walk toward a sunlit garden, while others climb steps toward a seated figure in a stone court.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:29, contrasting the resurrection of life for those who have done good with the resurrection of judgment for those who have done evil. The tombs recall the preceding verse; the garden, court, appearances, and setting are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A sunlit stone pool divided by a covered central walkway and surrounded by four roofed, columned porticoes, with sheep beside a gate in Jerusalem's city wall.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative view of the pool by Jerusalem's Sheep Gate, which John 5:2 describes as having five porticoes. The layout, architecture, and sheep are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, looking upward and extending an open hand toward several people. A balanced bronze scale stands on a low table beside Him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:30: Jesus judges as He hears, and His judgment is just because He seeks the will of the One who sent Him rather than His own. The courtyard, people, and balance are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward his chest while speaking to listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard; his face is reflected in a basin of water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative teaching scene uses the gesture and reflection to evoke John 5:31's conditional statement about Jesus bearing witness concerning Himself and His testimony not being true. The courtyard and reflection are artistic details, not details specified in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and gestures as a group of listeners gathers around him in a sunlit stone courtyard, with an archway and greenery behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Jesus speaking about the true testimony another bears concerning him. The sunlight is a visual suggestion, not a depiction or identification of the witness.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing rough brown clothing, gestures toward three listening men on a sunlit riverbank.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 5:33 says people were sent to John and that he bore witness to the truth. This imaginative scene shows him speaking with them beside the Jordan.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard and gestures with an open hand while several people listen; a path leads toward a city gate behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:34: Jesus says he does not receive testimony from a person, but speaks these things so that his listeners may be saved. The setting and poses are imagined. The relationship follows the pinned Greek text and Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing a rough brown garment, speaks to a smiling gathering around a burning oil lamp set on a stone at dusk.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' description of John as a burning, shining lamp and of people rejoicing for a time in his light. The gathering and physical lamp visualize the metaphor rather than document an event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands beside a pool as a smiling man carries a rolled mat and onlookers watch.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined moment connects Jesus' statement that the works the Father gave him testify that the Father sent him with the healing and carried mat earlier in John 5.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on stone steps in a sunlit courtyard, gesturing as five men listen; leafy vines and distant hillside buildings frame the gathering.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus addressing listeners as he speaks of the Father who sent him and bore witness about him. John 5:37 says they have neither heard the Father's voice nor seen his form. The chapter's word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to a group in a sunlit stone courtyard; one listener turns away while holding a rolled scroll.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:38: God’s word does not abide in the listeners, who do not believe the one He sent. The relationship follows the verse’s Berean Interlinear token glosses; the scene is not presented as a recorded historical event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward an unrolled scroll as four listeners gather around it in a sunlit stone courtyard with vines and greenery.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:39: Jesus speaks of people searching the Scriptures because they think they have eternal life in them, and says that the Scriptures bear witness concerning him. The English token glosses used for this interpretation are from the Berean Interlinear Bible and are marked uncurated in the lesson data, not GBT-approved.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: People rest on woven mats beneath stone colonnades beside a pool; a man leans on crutches, an older man holds a walking staff, and a woman lies near the water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the multitude of ailing people lying near the pool in John 5:3 and awaiting the movement of the water. The awaiting phrase falls within a passage marked with parentheses in the pinned Nestle 1904 text.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus extends an open hand toward four listeners who stand apart with their gazes lowered or turned away, in a sunlit stone courtyard beside flowers, greenery, and flowing water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene illustrates John 5:40: Jesus speaks of people who are unwilling to come to him to have life. The courtyard, garden, and water are artistic choices, with the living plants and water suggesting life.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus raises an open hand toward a man offering a laurel wreath while other men watch in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the offered wreath as a symbol of human glory, which Jesus says he does not receive in John 5:41. The wreath and courtyard are illustrative details, not events stated in the verse. The token glosses used are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus gestures toward a group of men, some sitting with folded arms or looking away.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 5:42, in which Jesus says that he knows his hearers and that they do not have the love of God in themselves. The courtyard, gestures, and expressions are artistic interpretation. The verse's English word glosses are from the uncurated Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus speaks with open hands while some listeners turn away; nearby, a richly dressed man gestures toward himself as smiling people welcome him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:43: Jesus says he has come in his Father's name and is not received, while another coming in his own name would be received. The second figure illustrates the verse's conditional contrast and is not an identification of a historical person. The verse relationship follows the Berean Interlinear token glosses in the source file, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus gestures toward the sky while one man places a leafy wreath on another and others watch.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene for John 5:44 uses a wreath to suggest receiving glory from one another and a gesture toward the light to suggest the glory from the only God that the listeners do not seek. The verse asks how they can believe; it does not describe the pictured event.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard. An imagined Moses stands behind them holding two blank tablets, while one listener holds a scroll.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:45: Jesus tells his listeners not to suppose that he will accuse them before the Father, because Moses, in whom they have hoped, is their accuser. Moses is shown as a visual evocation, not as a claim that he was physically present.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a blank scroll held by a listener as others gather around him in a sunlit stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene illustrates John 5:46, where Jesus connects believing Moses with believing him because Moses wrote about him. The courtyard, listeners, and scroll are artistic choices, not details specified in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to a group of listeners beside an unmarked scroll on a low table in a sunny stone courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: In this imaginative scene, the blank scroll represents Moses' writings as Jesus asks how his listeners will believe his words if they do not believe those writings. The chapter's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: An angel with glowing wings stirs a stone pool as a man steps into the water, while other people wait beside the pool beneath a colonnade.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the angel stirring the pool and the first person entering after the stirring, whom John 5:4 describes as made well. Nestle 1904 prints John 5:3-4 in parentheses; the English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man reclines on a woven mat beside a sunlit pool beneath stone colonnades, while others rest in the shade behind him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 5:5 describes a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years. This imaginative scene places him beside the pool and colonnades described in the surrounding passage.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus kneels beside a man lying on a mat and speaks to him near a pool surrounded by stone colonnades.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 5:6, when Jesus sees a man who has been ill a long time lying down and asks whether he wants to become well. The pool and colonnade draw on the surrounding passage.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Beside a stone pool, an ailing man on a mat gestures toward a person entering the water while Jesus listens; others sit beneath a sunlit colonnade.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene brings the man's account of having no one to put him into the stirred water, and of another going down before him, into his conversation with Jesus in John 5:7. It does not claim that these actions occurred at the same moment.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a man rising beside a stone pool and reaching for a woven mat; other people rest beneath the colonnade behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays Jesus instructing the man in John 5:8 to arise, take up his mat, and walk. The setting, poses, and appearances are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man walks beside a stone-lined pool, carrying a rolled woven mat under his arm while people gather beneath sunlit colonnades.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts John 5:9, when the man immediately became well, took up his mat and began to walk on the Sabbath. The pool and porticoes come from the surrounding account in John 5:2; their appearance and the figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a large crowd of men reclining on a grassy hillside, with a lake and distant hills beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 6:10: Jesus asks for the people to recline in a place with much grass, and about five thousand men recline. The setting, appearances, and arrangement are imagined. The chapter's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible; they are uncurated and are not GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus holds a basket of loaves and offers bread to a reclining man while a crowd shares bread and fish on a flowered hillside near the water.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 6:11: after giving thanks, Jesus distributes the loaves and likewise fish to those reclining, as much as they wished. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation. The chapter identifies the English word glosses as Berean Interlinear glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward his disciples as they gather pieces of bread into a woven basket on a grassy hillside, with the crowd and a lake behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative view of John 6:12, when Jesus tells his disciples to gather the remaining fragments after the people have eaten their fill, so that nothing is lost. The setting and visual details are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunny lakeside hillside, people gather pieces of bread into woven baskets: eleven baskets rest on the grass and another is carried by a man.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 6:13: twelve baskets are filled with fragments left from the five barley loaves after people had eaten. The verse relationship follows the chapter's Berean Interlinear glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man gestures toward Jesus among a crowd on a grassy lakeside hillside, with baskets of bread fragments in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene interprets John 6:14, when people speak of Jesus as the prophet after seeing the sign he performed. The baskets of bread fragments recall the feeding and gathering described in John 6:11-13. The English token glosses in the source are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks alone up a sunlit, rocky mountainside while a crowd gathers below, one person holding up a crown. A lake and hills lie in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus withdrawing to the mountain alone after realizing that the people intended to seize him and make him king. The crown and landscape are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Disciples walk down a rocky hillside toward a lakeshore, where boats rest in the warm light of sunset.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:16, in which Jesus' disciples go down to the sea as evening comes. The landscape, figures, and boats are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group of disciples in a wooden boat crosses a moonlit lake, rowing toward the lights of a distant shore.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of John 6:17: the disciples cross the sea toward Capernaum after dark, before Jesus has come to them. The moon, distant lights, and details of the boat are artistic choices. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: People aboard a wooden sailing boat grip ropes and its sides as foaming waves surge around them beneath a dark sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 6:18 describes the sea becoming agitated as a strong wind blows. This imaginative scene places the disciples' boat from the preceding passage amid the waves; the visual details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At night, frightened disciples in a wooden rowing boat look toward Jesus, who is walking on the waves near them beneath a moonlit sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:19: after rowing about twenty-five or thirty stadia, the disciples see Jesus walking on the sea and coming near their boat, and they are frightened. Their appearance, the boat, and the moonlit setting are artistic choices. The scene is informed by the verse's Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a wooden sailing boat on blue water, looking toward a sunlit shore with hills and a small town.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Jesus going across the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias, in John 6:1. The boat, shoreline, and weather are artistic choices; the verse does not describe them.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands on choppy moonlit water with open hands, addressing disciples who look toward him from a lantern-lit wooden boat.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:20, when Jesus reassures the disciples and tells them not to fear. John 6:18–19 supplies the setting of the wind, sea and boat. The chapter identifies its English token glosses as Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among welcoming disciples in a wooden fishing boat beside a rocky shore on a moonlit night.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene guided by the chapter's Berean Interlinear token glosses: the disciples are willing to receive Jesus into the boat, and the boat is at the land toward which they were going. The night and rough water recall the preceding verses; the figures and moonlit shore are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A crowd in robes gathers beneath trees on the shore of a blue lake, talking and looking toward a single distant wooden boat near the opposite shore.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative view of the crowd on the next day as they consider the one boat and realize that the disciples had departed without Jesus. The distant boat's position and the crowd's gestures are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several wooden sailboats carrying people approach a rocky lakeshore where people watch beneath a tree, with a basket of bread in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts boats from Tiberias arriving near the place where people had eaten bread after the Lord gave thanks; the basket evokes that earlier meal.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A crowd in robes arrives in wooden boats beside a lakeside village; some step onto the rocky shore while others look toward the houses.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 6:24, in which the crowd travels by boat to Capernaum seeking Jesus after finding neither him nor his disciples. The appearance of the people and setting is artistic interpretation. The verse's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands on a sunlit lakeshore as a man faces Him with open hands and several people look on; wooden boats, blue water, and a village appear behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 6:25, where the crowd finds Jesus on the other side of the sea and asks when He came there. The lakeshore setting, gestures, and appearances are artistic details. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a gathering beside the Sea of Galilee. Several people hold pieces of bread, and a nearly empty basket sits among them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 6:26, where Jesus says the people seek him because they ate the loaves and were satisfied rather than because they saw signs. The setting and visual details are artistic choices. The verse's English token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear; they are not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among listeners on a flowered hillside above a lake, holding out a loaf as sunlight falls around him; a basket of aging fruit and bread rests in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene for John 6:27 uses the offered loaf and aging food to suggest the contrast between perishable food and the enduring food the Son of Man gives for eternal life. The light on Jesus suggests the Father's seal on him. These are visual metaphors, not a literal account. The word glosses are the uncurated Berean Interlinear glosses associated with the Nestle 1904 text, not GBT-approved glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard overlooking a lake and hills, a man gestures with open hands toward Jesus while several people look on.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the question in John 6:28: the people ask Jesus what they should do to carry out the works of God. The setting and gestures are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. The wording follows the verse's Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, seated beneath a tree, speaks with an open hand to a circle of attentive listeners beside a lake. Boats, village buildings, and hills appear in the sunlit background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 6:29, where Jesus answers that the work of God is to believe in the one God sent. The lakeside setting and people's appearances are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches toward a seated ill man supported by a woman as a large crowd follows along a sunny lakeside path.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of John 6:2: a large crowd followed Jesus because they were seeing the signs he was doing on those who were sick. The individual encounter and setting are artistic choices; the word glosses used are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a man gestures with open hands toward a seated Jesus as several others look on.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:30, where people ask Jesus what sign and work he will perform so they may see and believe him. The setting, poses, and appearances are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Adults and children gather and eat small white pieces of manna from the rocky ground, carrying woven baskets beside a wilderness encampment at sunrise.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the ancestors' wilderness meal recalled in John 6:31, where the speakers say they ate manna and quote that bread from heaven was given to them.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits teaching a group beside a lake, raising his hand toward sunlight in the sky; a loaf rests in a basket nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of Jesus' words in John 6:32: his Father gives the true bread from heaven, in contrast to Moses. The lakeside setting, gestures, and basket of bread are artistic interpretation, not details stated in this verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, lit by a shaft of sunlight, offers a round loaf to a child and other people gathered on a flower-filled hillside overlooking a village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses Jesus offering bread and light descending from the sky to evoke John 6:33: the bread of God is the One coming down from heaven and giving life to the world. It is not a depiction of a specific event described in the verse. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone room, a man gestures with open hands toward Jesus as others listen; a loaf rests on a cloth-covered table.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the people asking Jesus to give them this bread always in John 6:34. The setting and loaf are artistic choices; the verse does not describe them. The English token glosses come from the file's uncurated Berean Interlinear layer.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree and speaks with open hands to a group of attentive listeners. A loaf of bread, a clay pitcher and a cup rest on a low table, with a lake and village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus' words that he is the bread of life: the one who comes to him will not hunger, and the one who believes in him will not thirst. The bread and water vessel are visual reminders; the setting and objects are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus in cream and red robes gestures toward five listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard. They look at Him with questioning expressions.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 6:36, where Jesus says His listeners have seen Him and yet do not believe. The courtyard and the listeners’ expressions are artistic choices, informed by the verse’s uncurated Berean Interlinear glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, wearing a cream robe and red shawl, extends his arms toward a man reaching out to him on a sunlit path. Several people approach behind the man, with a lake and village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus welcoming someone who comes to him, reflecting his promise that all the Father gives him will come and that he will never cast out the one who comes. The English word glosses consulted are the uncurated Berean Interlinear glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward sunlight in the sky while teaching a group on a hillside overlooking a lake and a stone village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 6:38, where Jesus says he came down from heaven to do the will of the One who sent him. The setting, listeners, and gesture are artistic choices. The source file's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit watercolor landscape, Jesus takes the hand of a woman rising beside an open rock-cut tomb while a group of men and women gathers around him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual meditation on John 6:39: Jesus preserves all that the One who sent him has given him and raises it on the last day. The figures and setting are artistic interpretation. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT-approved translation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and gestures among his disciples on a sunlit, flower-dotted rocky hillside. A path rises behind them, and a blue lake, village, and distant hills fill the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:3, in which Jesus goes up the mountain and sits there with his disciples; the landscape and figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus clasps the hand of a man rising beside an open rock-hewn tomb, while people watch among flowers in a sunlit landscape.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative picture of the Father's will that those who behold and believe in the Son have eternal life, and of Jesus' promise to raise them on the last day.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a gathered group in a sunlit stone room while one listener whispers to another; a round loaf rests on the table.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering portrays the listeners grumbling about Jesus as he speaks. The loaf is a visual reminder of his statement that he is the bread that came down from heaven, not an additional action described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone village courtyard, four people in period robes look toward Jesus; one gestures toward him and another raises a hand toward the sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined conversation illustrates John 6:42: people question how Jesus, whom they identify as Joseph's son and whose father and mother they know, can say that he came down from heaven. The courtyard, gestures and sunlight are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a gathering in a sunlit stone courtyard while one man whispers to another and others listen.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus answering the people and telling them not to grumble among one another in John 6:43. The setting and visual details are artistic choices; the source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gently helps a man rise beside an open rock-hewn tomb, with warm dawn light crossing an olive-covered hillside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual metaphor for John 6:44: heavenly light suggests the Father drawing a person to Jesus, and rising beside the tomb suggests Jesus’ promise to raise that person on the last day. This is not a claim that the pictured event was witnessed.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group of people walk toward Jesus along a sunlit Galilean path as he welcomes them with open hands. One person carries a rolled scroll.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 6:45: those who hear and learn from the Father come to Jesus. The sunlight and scroll are visual symbols, not details the verse describes.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits teaching a group of listeners in a sunlit stone room, looking upward and gesturing. An open doorway reveals a lake and distant hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus teaching about the Father. John 6:46 says that no one has seen the Father except the One who is from God; the Father is not depicted.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and gestures while teaching several attentive listeners in a sunlit room; an olive tree and a village are visible through the open doorway.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 6:47's assurance that the one believing has eternal life. The sunlit olive tree suggests life; it is not a detail stated in the verse. The verse's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he teaches four listeners around a low table with a round loaf and pottery in a sunlit stone courtyard overlooking a lakeside village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses a loaf as a visual reminder of Jesus' declaration that he is the bread of life. The particular courtyard, loaf, and listeners are artistic additions, not details specified in John 6:48.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A family eats pale manna in a sunlit wilderness camp while an elder sits thoughtfully beside a small mound of stones.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 6:49's words that the fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died. The stone mound suggests mortality without implying that the manna caused their deaths.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman and a child prepare flatbread in a stone courtyard beside baskets of herbs, while a lamb stands nearby and a path winds toward a sunlit village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The chapter's uncurated Berean Interlinear glosses describe Passover, the feast of the Jews, as near. This imagined household and its preparations evoke the approaching feast; the verse does not describe them.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus offers torn bread to a seated listener holding a piece, while others gather on a sunlit hillside overlooking a lake.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses Jesus offering bread and light descending from the sky to evoke His words about the bread coming down from heaven, which one may eat and not die. The setting and gathering are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among attentive listeners on a sunlit hillside, offering a broken loaf with one hand and placing the other over his heart. Golden light falls over greenery, a lake, distant hills, and a village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses bread, descending light, and Jesus' gesture to evoke John 6:51: he is the living bread from heaven and will give his flesh for the life of the world. The verse does not describe this particular gathering or action.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jewish listeners exchange questioning looks and open-handed gestures around Jesus, who stands calmly beside them, with a lakeside village in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the listeners arguing over how Jesus could give them flesh to eat, as reflected in the Berean Interlinear word glosses for John 6:52. The setting and gestures are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree, gesturing as a group listens beside a lake. A broken loaf, a cup of red drink, and grapes rest on a cloth in the foreground.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 6:53: Jesus teaches while bread and a cup evoke his words that unless people eat the Son of Man's flesh and drink his blood, they have no life in themselves. The setting and objects are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: At sunrise, Jesus clasps a man's hand and helps him rise beside a rock-hewn tomb. The man holds bread, and a cup of red wine rests on a nearby stone.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses bread and a cup to evoke Jesus' words about eating his flesh and drinking his blood. Jesus helping the man rise evokes his promise of eternal life and of raising that person on the last day in John 6:54.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward himself as he speaks to listeners around a wooden table holding a broken loaf and a cup of red wine, in a sunlit room overlooking a distant lakeside village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses bread and a cup to evoke Jesus' words in John 6:55: his flesh is true food and his blood is true drink. The verse itself does not describe this particular gathering.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits with his arm around a disciple who holds broken bread and a cup of red wine, at a table in a sunlit stone courtyard overlooking a lake.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined meal uses bread and a cup to evoke Jesus' words about eating his flesh and drinking his blood, while the closeness of Jesus and the disciple suggests his promise of mutual abiding. The verse does not describe this particular meal.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus holds bread and gestures toward a listener holding a piece near his mouth in a sunlit stone courtyard overlooking a lake.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses bread and sunlight to evoke John 6:57: Jesus says the living Father sent him and he lives because of the Father, and the one feeding on him will live because of him. The setting and gestures are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus teaches a group beneath a tree, gesturing toward the sunlit sky. A loaf rests on a low table, with stone tombs visible in the distant hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the loaf, sunlight, living tree, and distant tombs to evoke Jesus's contrast in John 6:58: the fathers ate and died, while the one who eats this bread will live into the age. The scene is a visual interpretation, not a recorded description of this moment.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and gestures as he teaches a gathering in a sunlit stone interior; buildings and water appear beyond the columns.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum, as described in John 6:59; the listeners and setting details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures while speaking with Philip on a grassy hillside as a large crowd approaches, with a lake and mountains beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:5, in which Jesus sees a great crowd coming and asks Philip where they can buy bread for the people to eat.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several disciples sit together in a sunlit stone room, one gesturing with open hands as others look troubled; Jesus teaches at a wooden stand in the background.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the disciples' response in John 6:60: after hearing Jesus, many describe the word as difficult and ask who can hear it. The synagogue at Capernaum follows the setting in John 6:59. The local English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a Global Bible Tools approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone hall, speaking with an open hand to His disciples; two whisper together while others listen with troubled expressions.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 6:61: knowing His disciples are grumbling about His teaching, Jesus asks whether it offends them. The setting and appearances are artistic choices. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus rises amid golden clouds as people on a hillside look up toward him; a lake and village lie in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visualization of Jesus' question in John 6:62 about seeing the Son of Man ascend to where he was before, not a claim that this scene occurred at that moment. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath an olive tree, speaking with open hands to a small group of listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard, with fresh greenery and a blue lake beyond.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined teaching scene inspired by John 6:63. The listeners and fresh greenery evoke Jesus' words that the Spirit gives life and that the words he has spoken are spirit and life. The verse's contrast with flesh that profits nothing is not depicted literally. The English word glosses used as guidance are from the uncurated Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a circle of listeners in a sunlit stone room; several look uncertain while one man stands apart, turned away.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 6:64, where Jesus knows from the beginning who does not believe and who will betray him. The setting, gestures, and expressions are artistic interpretation. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and speaks to a man standing with open hands beneath a shaft of golden light, while others listen in a stone courtyard overlooking Galilean hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene for John 6:65 uses the light to suggest the Father's granting of a person's coming to Jesus as Jesus teaches his listeners. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a group of disciples walking away along a sunlit path, while a few remain with Him among rocks and olive trees above a lakeside village.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 6:66, where many of Jesus' disciples went back and no longer walked with Him. The setting, people, and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, extending an open hand as twelve disciples gather around him; a path winds toward distant hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts Jesus asking the Twelve whether they also wish to go away in John 6:67. The courtyard, gestures, and landscape are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Simon Peter sits and gestures with an open hand toward Jesus as nearby disciples listen; several figures walk away in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 6:68, where Peter asks to whom they would go and says Jesus has the words of eternal life. The setting and gestures are imagined; the departing figures evoke the preceding verses. English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Peter gestures toward Jesus as several disciples gather around them beside the Sea of Galilee, with stone buildings, fishing boats, and hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of Peter speaking for the disciples as they confess that they have believed and known Jesus to be the Holy One of God in John 6:69. The lakeside setting and appearances are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warm watercolor scene, Jesus speaks with an open gesture to a thoughtful Philip as they sit on a grassy hillside. A crowd approaches behind them, with a blue lake and mountains in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Jesus speaking to test Philip, while already knowing what he was about to do. The approaching crowd and question about bread come from the preceding verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath an olive tree, speaking with open hands to twelve attentive disciples on a rocky hillside, with a village and distant hills behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering illustrates Jesus asking the Twelve whether he chose them and saying that one of them is a devil. The setting and shadow are artistic details, and the scene does not identify an individual.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward seated disciples in a sunlit stone courtyard, while a thoughtful Judas sits slightly apart on a step beneath olive branches.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus speaking with disciples, with Judas set apart in quiet reflection. The verse identifies Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, as one of the Twelve who was about to betray him; the illustration does not show all twelve disciples.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Philip gestures toward a large crowd while speaking to Jesus on a grassy hillside above the Sea of Galilee; a small purse and loaf lie nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Philip explaining that even two hundred denarii worth of bread would not give each person in the crowd a little. The loaf and purse are visual additions, not details stated in John 6:7. The source word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Andrew gestures while speaking to Jesus on a grassy hillside overlooking the Sea of Galilee. Other disciples listen nearby, and a crowd approaches in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Andrew, whom John 6:8 identifies as Simon Peter's brother, speaking to Jesus. The appearances and visual details are imagined. The chapter file attributes its English token glosses to the Berean Interlinear Bible; they are not a GBT approval.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A boy sits with a basket holding five barley loaves and two small fish while a thoughtful man gestures beside him, with a crowd spread across a sunlit lakeside hillside.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the little boy with five barley loaves and two small fish in John 6:9; the crowd suggests the question of what these are for so many. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks alone along a rocky uphill path, behind a group of men approaching a crowd and tents near a sunlit ancient city.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:10: after his brothers went up to the feast, Jesus also went up, not openly but as if in secret. The setting, route, appearance and gathering are artistic choices. The excerpt's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard filled with feast-goers, a group gestures and asks an older man while people gather among fabric canopies, baskets, and food.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined festival scene reflects John 7:11, whose Berean Interlinear word glosses describe the Jews seeking him at the feast and asking where he is. The individual people, gestures, and surroundings are artistic additions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone town, people in robes converse in small groups: some smile as they speak, while others look doubtful. Jesus stands among people in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 7:12, where crowds murmur about Jesus: some say he is good, while others accuse him of deceiving the people. The setting, expressions, and Jesus' visible presence are artistic choices. The verse relationship follows the excerpt's Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four worried people sit together in a sunlit stone courtyard; one man whispers to a woman while their companions glance toward passersby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 7:13: the supplied Berean Interlinear glosses say that no one was speaking publicly about him because of fear of the Jews. The courtyard, people and whispered exchange are imagined, not details specified by the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus teaches a group seated on stone steps in a sunlit temple court, with feastgoers and colorful canopies behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:14, in which Jesus goes up to the temple and teaches in the middle of the feast. The people and visual details are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A seated man gestures while six listeners look on in surprise in a sunlit stone courtyard; a closed scroll rests nearby.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:15: listeners marvel and ask how the man knows writings without having studied, following the excerpt's Berean Interlinear glosses. The courtyard, scroll, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, speaking with an open hand and pointing upward while four listeners watch.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts Jesus answering his listeners. His upward gesture suggests his words in John 7:16: his teaching is from the one who sent him.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus teaches a group in a sunlit stone courtyard while a listener offers a cup to a seated man and looks toward Jesus.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined moment relates to John 7:17: the listener's readiness to act and attention to Jesus' teaching evoke the verse's connection between desiring to do God's will and knowing whether the teaching comes from God. The courtyard and the sharing of water are imaginative details, not events described in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a seated teacher extends one hand toward the distant light as listeners gather, while another speaker at the side gestures toward his own chest.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined contrast illustrates John 7:18: one who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, while the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true and without unrighteousness. The scene is an artistic interpretation, not an event stated in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus sits with one hand extended toward several listeners, some attentive and others wary. A rolled parchment rests on a stone table.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes Jesus' words about Moses giving the law, the failure to keep it, and his question about why his listeners seek to kill him. The courtyard and scroll are artistic details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a sunlit path among trees and wildflowers, with a lake and village beyond and a shadowed road leading toward a distant hilltop settlement.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus walking in Galilee. The verse says he did not wish to walk in Judea because people were seeking to kill him; the landscape and shadowed road are an artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus faces a crowd whose members gesture toward him with puzzled and questioning expressions.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests the crowd's response in John 7:20. The excerpt's Berean Interlinear word glosses present an accusation and a question about who seeks to kill the person addressed.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, raising one finger as he speaks to a group of attentive, wondering listeners.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus answering listeners who marvel at the one work he says he did; the particular work is not identified in this verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A teacher speaks to a family in a sunlit courtyard, while a woman cradles a swaddled baby beside an elder holding a closed scroll.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative gathering and swaddled infant suggest the ancestral practice of circumcision. John 7:22 says Moses gave circumcision, though it came from the fathers, and speaks of circumcising a man on the Sabbath. The verse does not describe this gathering or a baby. The reading follows the supplied Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a standing man as several listeners look on in a sunlit stone courtyard; a closed scroll rests on a table.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of Jesus' question in John 7:23 about anger at making a whole man well on the Sabbath, while circumcision is received on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken. The courtyard and visual details are artistic additions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, an elder listens to two men, one in fine clothes and one in worn clothes, as they gesture around a table holding a tied bundle and a small balance scale.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hearing illustrates the verse's call to judge righteously rather than according to appearance. The people and circumstances are artistic inventions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, several residents confer with worried expressions and gesture toward a robed man standing a little distance away.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 7:25, where some Jerusalem residents ask whether this is the man whom others seek to kill. The courtyard, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a crowd in a sunlit stone courtyard while rulers watch quietly and two listeners exchange questioning glances.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 7:26: Jesus speaks publicly without a response, while listeners wonder whether the rulers have recognized Him as the Christ. The courtyard, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices, and the rulers' recognition remains a question.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus in a red mantle stands among talking townspeople in a sunlit stone courtyard, while a man looks toward a winding road and distant hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests the speakers' claim that they know where this man is from and their expectation that no one will know where the Christ comes from. The courtyard, road and figures are artistic interpretations.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with one hand raised as listeners gather around him in a sunlit temple courtyard.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus crying out while teaching in the temple, as he speaks of the true One who sent him, whom his listeners do not know. The courtyard, gestures and listeners are artistic interpretation of John 7:28.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among attentive listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard, one hand on his chest and the other raised toward the sky.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects Jesus saying that he knows the One from whom he comes and who sent him; the courtyard and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A man arranges leafy branches over a wooden booth while a woman and child hold more greenery; other villagers prepare shelters among sunlit stone buildings.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 7:2 says the Jewish Feast of Booths was near. This imagined village preparation suggests its approach; the verse does not describe these people or their actions.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands in a sunlit stone courtyard while several men reach toward him without touching him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard scene reflects John 7:30: people sought to take him, yet no one laid a hand on him because his hour had not yet come. The excerpt's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks among a crowd in a sunlit stone courtyard. Many people look toward him while two men in the foreground speak together.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects the crowd believing in Jesus and speaking about whether the coming Christ would do more signs than he has already done. The setting and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, robed religious leaders gesture to departing officers while people converse around Jesus in the crowd.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene follows John 7:32 as the Berean Interlinear word glosses present it: Pharisees hear the crowd murmuring about Jesus, and the chief priests and Pharisees send officers to seize Him. The setting, clothing, and arrangement of figures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to listeners seated in a sunlit stone courtyard, with a path winding toward a distant village and hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene relates to John 7:33, where Jesus tells his listeners he is with them for a little while and is going to the One who sent him. The courtyard and path are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several people search among stone village paths while a distant figure of Jesus stands on a sunlit hillside beyond a deep ravine.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual metaphor for John 7:34: the searchers and the ravine suggest seeking without finding and being unable to come where Jesus is. The landscape is imagined, not a depicted historical location.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four Jewish men in robes converse in a sunlit stone courtyard; one gestures toward a winding road and a distant harbor with classical buildings.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of the questions in John 7:35. The distant road and harbor suggest the possibility the speakers discuss: that he might go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks. The verse presents this as a question.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A group in robes exchanges puzzled looks and open-handed gestures in a sunlit stone courtyard while a distant figure walks away through an arch.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene reflects the question about the saying that people will seek the speaker without finding him and cannot come where he is. The setting, gestures, and departing figure are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open arms and speaks to a gathering in a sunlit stone courtyard. A man holding a cup moves toward Him as the others listen beneath leafy branches.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 7:37: on the great last day of the feast, Jesus stands and calls out, inviting anyone who thirsts to come to Him and drink. The courtyard, listeners and cup are imagined details.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a believer under a tree as clear streams flow from the believer's clothed midsection into a green valley.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:38, picturing the rivers of living water that the verse says will flow from within the one who believes in Jesus.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on stone steps in a sunlit courtyard, speaking with an open hand to five attentive listeners. Vines frame the scene, with a village and hills in the distance.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests Jesus speaking to people who believe in him as they await the Spirit. John 7:39 explains that they were to receive the Spirit and that the Spirit had not yet been given because Jesus had not yet been glorified; the setting and figures are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus listens to two men in robes beside a stone house and olive trees, as one gestures toward a winding road through sunlit hills.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:3, where Jesus' brothers urge him to leave for Judea so that his disciples may see the works he is doing. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a bearded teacher in cream and red robes addresses a crowd. In the foreground, one listener points toward him as others speak together.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:40: after hearing the words, some in the crowd say that he truly is the Prophet. The setting, expressions, and gestures are imagined; the supplied word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, people gather around a man in pale robes. One man gestures eagerly toward him, while another raises a hand and rests his other hand on his chin.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 7:41: some say the man is the Christ, while others question whether the Christ comes from Galilee. The courtyard, people, and gestures are imagined.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Four people discuss a blank scroll beneath an old olive tree as one gestures toward a distant stone village; a fresh shoot grows near the tree's roots and a solitary traveler walks the road.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects the verse's question about Scripture saying that the Christ comes from David's line and Bethlehem, where David was. The olive shoot and traveler are visual symbols, not events stated in the verse.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus stands calmly while clusters of people gesture and speak with differing expressions.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 7:43's account of a division in the crowd because of Jesus; the setting, appearance, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands calmly in a sunlit stone courtyard while several men face him with tense expressions; some hold out their hands without touching him.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 7:44: some wanted to seize Jesus, but no one laid hands on him. The setting and gestures are artistic choices. The verse relationship follows the excerpt's Berean Interlinear word glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Three armored officers face robed chief priests and Pharisees in a sunlit stone courtyard, while a leader gestures toward them with an open hand.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 7:45, where the officers come to the chief priests and Pharisees, who ask why they did not bring him. It follows the supplied Berean Interlinear glosses; the courtyard, clothing, and gestures are artistic choices.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Three officers in a sunlit stone courtyard answer a group of listeners, one gesturing with open hands, while a man speaks to an attentive gathering behind them.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the officers answering that no one has spoken as this man speaks; the courtyard and arrangement of the figures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a robed Pharisee gestures with open hands while other Pharisees and a seated group listen.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined setting for John 7:47, in which the Pharisees answer a group by asking whether they too have been deceived. The courtyard, figures, and gestures are artistic choices; the verse does not specify them. The wording is informed by the excerpt's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Several robed men gather in a sunlit stone courtyard as a seated elder gestures and the others listen thoughtfully.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined gathering gives visual form to the verse's question, expressed through the supplied Berean Interlinear token glosses, about whether any rulers or Pharisees believed in him. The setting and gestures are imaginative and do not settle the question.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit ancient courtyard, a stern robed man holding a rolled scroll gestures toward a crowd of men and women who watch him with concerned or thoughtful expressions.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene suggests the accusation in John 7:49 that the crowd does not know the law and is accursed. The setting, speaker, scroll, gestures and reactions are artistic interpretations, not details specified by the verse. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men converse in a shaded stone doorway; one gestures toward a sunlit square where people walk among stone buildings.
records_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined conversation uses a shaded doorway and a public square to suggest the verse's contrast between acting in secret and showing oneself to the world. The setting and gestures are artistic interpretation.

records_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed Nicodemus gestures as he speaks among a group of men in a warmly lit stone room.
